analyst_view.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points) three days before Sunday's Klassieker at Feyenoord. Ajax have won six of their last seven, but lost midfielder Jorthy Mokio to a broken fibula against ADO Den Haag (out until about late February), which the numbers' empty missing list does not know; Brandt, Amrabat and Gaaei are back, while Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov are long-term absences already in Ajax's form. A Dutch preview from Tuesday expects Míchel to rest Julian Brandt and keep Oscar Gloukh for Feyenoord, so a partly changed Ajax attack is likely even though Míchel called Thun an important game. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys, miss defenders Montolio and Saiz long-term, and Sports Mole and Blick-based reports say striker Furkan Dursun (back) and midfielder Mattias Käit (back) are not expected to make it; coach Gian-Luca Privitelli also faces three games in a week after this and may rotate. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, with Ajax expected to score 3.2 on their strong recent form. They don't know Mokio is out, a Dutch preview expects Brandt to be rested and Gloukh saved for the Klassieker, and Thun's main striker Dursun looks set to miss out, so both attacks are a bit weaker than the numbers assume; I go to about 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, most of them (6.5) for Ajax, who will dominate the ball at home against a Thun side that sits back away from home. A changed Ajax front line still plays the same wide game, so nothing here moves the corner count; I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.7) as the side chasing the ball. No referee has been named, there is no history between the clubs, and Thun's defender Dähler says they come to take points rather than to sit and foul, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots, about 20 of them for Ajax. With Brandt likely rested, Mokio out and Gloukh possibly saved for Feyenoord, plus Thun missing striker Dursun, I trim slightly to about 29.6; it is a mild lean because Ajax should still have most of the ball.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Ajax's likely rotation of their most creative players before the Klassieker and Thun's loss of their main striker both cut the quality of chances a little, which the numbers can't see, so I go to about 9.2.
